_readme: Resume↔site drift guard (wave 13 follow-up). Each claim maps a metric the resume PDF states to its content/metrics.json id, recording the STORE value at the moment the resume was last synced. The weekly metrics-refresh workflow flags any claim whose store value has moved since sync (the resume shouldn't silently rot while the site self-heals), and flags a public/resume.pdf hash change without a manifest update (a resume swap that skipped this file). Regenerate this file whenever the resume is rebuilt: update resume_says/store_value_at_sync per claim, resume_pdf_sha256, and synced_at. Claims derived from site code (e.g. the 'Nine live AI products' count = liveProductCount) are not tracked here — they have no store id.

warmer:hinglish-fix.resume_says: Spearman −0.003 → 0.813, held-out 0.435 → 0.704 (LoRA fine-tune published as hinglish-relatedness-sbert)

triageiq:classifier-top3.resume_says: component classifier top-3 accuracy 87.1% (k8s) / 89.8% (vscode); CQR conformal coverage 76.2% / 74.6% vs. an 80% target

mmfr:recall10.resume_says: Recall@10 3.06× over a popularity baseline (0.0328 vs 0.0107)

aetherart:vram.resume_says: full pipeline at 6.2GB peak VRAM against an 8GB budget

reviewiq:extraction-eval.resume_says: 78.6% extraction accuracy on a 43-review eval (95% CI 73–83%)

agentgauge:blocking-causal.resume_says: BLOCKING description defect measured at −13.3 to −28.9pp agent task success (3 model families)

gold-rate-tracker:headline.resume_says: the forecaster that ships its naive baseline, because the baseline honestly beat the model
